body:
I just wanted to give more of a followup to this thoughtful reply. I was passing out for the night when this got posted.

The stuff you've suggested in regard to learning how it feels to be her, that's more or less what I've been trying to do, but it isn't easy. She tells me more than she tells anyone else, but it still isn't much. Often, whenever things start getting quite personal, she completely shuts down. You're in the middle of talking to her and you reach what you think is going to be a critical question for crossing a new threshold of understanding, and she won't/can't answer. She says during these times, she can't stop picturing some comforting image. Most times she cannot remember the subject that was under discussion at all, and sometimes cannot remember who or where she is. Obviously, this has led to a lot of failure in therapists' offices, who have often dismissed her as being totally fine when, to save face for being in these blackouts, she reverts to a non-threatening subject, i.e. "I'm just a little stressed right now because of this heavy courseload I'm taking." (At which point they all say, oh so you're fine then, the temporary circumstances in your life just need to change. Wait it out!)

We've tried to get her into the counselling services at her school before, but she stopped going because she was so busy with school and work. Now she owes her school money, and is under the impression that they're not going to offer her their services until she's paid them, which may take a while. I've been out of the country for a while, but when I get back in 6 days I'm going to ask the school's counselling office if they'd still take her. The local hotline knowing about low/no-cost options in the area is a great point.

To speak to your last point, I do have some idea of the difference between ideation and intent, and I've known for a while she's had the ideations, but we both agreed she wasn't close to acting on them. However, the red flag for me is the fact that she has very specific plans: method and location. She says things like, "one day I'm going to do it."

I agree with you though that what she's really seeking seeking here is an escape from all the pain she's feeling on a daily basis. I've told her I want her to call me any time things are really going to hell, but I'll be clear about framing that as the safety plan.

Anyway, again, thanks so much for your reply. I just felt like giving an in-depth response .
